title: Why Isn't IBM's Stock Bouncing Back After Strong Earnings Results?
detail:
Why Isn't IBM's Stock Bouncing Back After Strong Earnings Results?
Patrick Sanders, The Motley Fool
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 11:17 AM MST 4 min read
IBM
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

In July, IBM (NYSE:IBM) stock suffered the worst day in its 115-year history, falling about 25% after the company warned that customers had shifted spending away from its products.

The miss was clearly a matter of timing -- a series of major contracts IBM was planning didn't close by the end of the quarter, as its customers shifted spending to memory and storage products whose prices were increasing rapidly.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Three months later, IBM's third-quarter report, which landed on Oct. 21, mostly backed that assessment up, and the company posted strong revenue and earnings. So, why isn't the stock bouncing back?

Image source: Getty Images.

The good news was real

IBM's revenue rose 5% to $17.1 billion in the third quarter, up from 1% growth in the second. Software grew 9% at constant currency, and operating earnings per share rose 11% to $2.95. Free cash flow was $3 billion, and management raised its full-year outlook to FCF growth of more than $1 billion.

CFO Jim Kavanaugh said about two-thirds of the large software deals that slipped in the second quarter closed in the third. Transaction processing software, which is tied to mainframes, swung from a 9% decline to 10% growth. That looks like delayed spending, not lost customers.

Some of that growth was bought

IBM closed its roughly $11 billion acquisition of Confluent in March, so that revenue wasn't included in last year's numbers. Confluent's last reported quarterly revenue was $314.8 million, and IBM's software revenue in Q3 2025 was $7.2 billion. So that would put IBM's organic software growth in this quarter at around 4%. That's real progress, but it's less dramatic than 9%.

Management is also tapping the brakes. CEO Arvind Krishna said he doesn't expect transaction processing to keep growing at double digits, and IBM expects that business to be flat for the year. Kavanaugh said the company is expecting about $32 billion in full-year software revenue. Subtract the $22.6 billion IBM has recognized through nine months, and the fourth quarter works out to roughly 4% growth, versus 8% in the third. Mainframe hardware sales also fell 20%, although that came against a very strong launch a year ago.

IBM is a long-term buy

I still like IBM as a long-term investment in AI and quantum computing, but I'm not ignoring the risks. IBM spent $11.4 billion on acquisitions this year, so cash fell $3.4 billion to $11.1 billion, and debt rose $2.6 billion to $63.8 billion. The dividend looks well covered -- IBM paid $4.8 billion of dividends against $7.8 billion of free cash flow through nine months -- but there's less cushion for another big deal. Meanwhile, shareholders receive a dividend yield of about 2.7%.

Hedera (CRYPTO:HBAR) needs a 209.6% increase to return to $0.25, a level it last reached on September 19, 2025. Investors are particularly attentive to this threshold because HBAR held that level for several weeks in mid-2025, closing July 2025 at about $0.251.

However, HBAR's price has moved downward. HBAR trades around $0.081, down 4.8% in 24 hours, 14.3% over the past two weeks, and 14.8% over the last month. Furthermore, it remains 85.8% below its all-time high of $0.57.

Furkan Cubuk / Shutterstock.com

In October, HBAR has fluctuated between $0.107 and $0.080 and trades barely above this month's low. This decline followed a surge to $0.131 in September. So, what would it take for HBAR to reach $0.25 again?

HBAR Needs an $11 Billion Market Cap to Hit $0.25
Akif CUBUK / Shutterstock.com

To understand HBAR's price target, look at market capitalization, which is calculated by multiplying the coin's price by the number of tokens in circulation. With a current market cap of about $3.56 billion, HBAR would need to rise to $0.25 to reach about $11 billion.

Unfortunately, the increasing supply of HBAR makes this challenge more daunting. Around 44 billion HBAR tokens are in circulation out of a maximum of 50 billion. This growing supply means reaching the same price level now requires significantly more buyer investment than when HBAR traded above $0.25 in 2021.

title: IBM (IBM) stock trades down, here is why
detail:
IBM (IBM) stock trades down, here is why
Jabin Bastian
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 9:21 AM MST 3 min read
IBM
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
What happened?

Shares of technology and consulting giant IBM (NYSE:IBM) fell 2.9% in the morning session after the company maintained its full-year constant-currency revenue growth forecast of 4% to 5%, overshadowing a third-quarter beat across both revenue and profit.

IBM reported third-quarter revenue of $17.1 billion, up 4.7% year on year, alongside adjusted earnings of $2.95 per share, according to the company's press release. Both prints exceeded Wall Street consensus estimates calling for $16.79 billion in revenue and adjusted earnings of $2.87 per share. Gains were driven by the software and infrastructure divisions, while IBM lifted its annual free cash flow expansion target to more than $1 billion.

On the earnings call, Chief Financial Officer Jim Kavanaugh noted that software acceleration was aided by closing approximately two-thirds of the large enterprise deals that slipped from the second quarter, driving a 10% rebound in Transaction Processing. Chief Executive Arvind Krishna highlighted strength across hybrid cloud and AI platforms, citing high-teens bookings growth at Red Hat and a 32% jump in Distributed Infrastructure as clients expanded data and storage capacity.Because much of the top-line beat stemmed from recovering delayed deals rather than fresh demand acceleration, keeping full-year sales guidance unchanged confirmed that the third-quarter surge pulled forward revenue rather than resetting the baseline. However, investors often look for raised guidance following a quarterly beat, and the decision to leave the revenue outlook unchanged appeared to weigh on the stock.

After the initial drop, the shares shed some of the losses and rose to $246.50, down 2% from the previous close.

The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks. Is now the time to buy IBM? Access our full analysis report here, it's free.

What is the market telling us

IBM's shares are quite volatile and have had 16 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today's move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 21 days ago when the stock gained 5.7% on the news that the company announced a self-hosted deployment option for IBM Bob, an agentic software development platform designed to advance enterprise artificial intelligence sovereignty and governance.

In a corporate release, IBM stated that the self-hosted deployment enables enterprises to run AI-driven software delivery and modernization inside customer-controlled environments, including on-premises systems, sovereign clouds, private clouds, and air-gapped environments. Additionally, IBM announced an expansion to its IBM Bob Premium Package for Z, incorporating the self-hosted capability along with deeper application intelligence tools. According to the company, these enhancements are designed to modernize mission-critical mainframe workloads while satisfying strict compliance and data sovereignty standards.

title: Why Did IBM Stock Beat Gartner Over Five Years?

Why Did IBM Stock Beat Gartner Over Five Years?
Trefis Team

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

Two companies in the same industry grew their sales at about the same pace over the last three years. Over the five years to October 2026, however, their stocks moved in opposite directions. International Business Machines (IBM) rose 147.2%, while Gartner (IT) fell 31.3%. Where would you guess the gap came from: faster sales, bigger profits, or investors paying more for those profits?

Who Has Beaten Gartner Over Five Years?

Gartner trailed most of its industry. Among the 28 companies in IT Consulting & Other Services, the median stock fell 23.5% over those five years. That decline was smaller than Gartner's 31.3% drop, though 12 peers recorded a lower return.

Three companies with similar sales growth beat Gartner by a wide margin: IBM, Adeia and Cognizant Technology Solutions (CTSH). The table shows the first two. IBM finished the five-year period 178.5 percentage points ahead of Gartner.

Adeia (ADEA) finished even further ahead, beating Gartner by 197.1 points. A weak industry is only part of Gartner's story. The stocks of IBM and Adeia more than doubled, even though both companies grew their sales within 4 points of Gartner's pace over three years.

Did IBM Grow Faster Than Gartner?

No. IBM and Gartner grew their sales at about the same pace over the last three years. IBM averaged 4.5% annual sales growth, while Gartner averaged 4.0%. The two companies sell different things. IBM sells software, including Red Hat, along with consulting and the servers and storage that run its clients' mission-critical work. Gartner mostly sells research for senior executives.

Faster sales growth is not where IBM's lead came from.

Where Did The Gap Come From?

Part of the gap came from the price investors pay for each dollar of profit. In June 2021, investors paid 36.3 times earnings for Gartner's stock and 23.6 times for IBM's. Today, they pay 18.8 times for Gartner, about half as much. IBM's multiple is little changed at 22.1 times, based on earnings through June, before IBM reported third-quarter results after the October 21 close. These multiples date from four months before the five-year price window starts, so they do not line up with the stock moves.

Profit per share rose 90.1% at IBM and 71.8% at Gartner between the twelve months to June 2021 and the twelve months to June 2026. IBM's net income more than doubled over the same span, rising 101.1%.

title: IBM's Strong Q3 Infrastructure Growth, Cost Savings Offset Weak Gross Margins, Morgan Stanley Says
detail:
PREMIUM
IBM's Strong Q3 Infrastructure Growth, Cost Savings Offset Weak Gross Margins, Morgan Stanley Says
MT Newswires
Thu, October 22, 2026 at 8:00 AM MST 1 min read
IBM
Trade IBM on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

IBM (IBM) rebounded in Q3, closing two-thirds of the deals that slipped in the previous quarter, while strong Distributed Infrastructure growth and operating expense savings helped offset gross margin pressure, Morgan Stanley said Thursday in a note.

The company reported Q3 adjusted EPS of $2.95 and revenue of $17.10 billion, both modestly above expectations. Q4 guidance for EPS of $4.55 to $4.60 and revenue of $20.3 billion was in-line to slightly below consensus estimates of $4.62 and $20.45 billion, respectively.

The brokerage does not expect the bull versus bear debate to change following Q3. Bulls point to growing momentum across several Software sub-segments, a thriving Infrastructure business and cost savings supporting EPS growth.

Bears, meanwhile, highlight low-single-digit organic Software growth that needs to improve significantly in 2027 and limited mergers and acquisitions activity, which is crucial to management's 5% revenue growth target in 2027, according to the note.

The brokerage raised its 2026 and 2027 EPS estimates to $12.43 and $13.46, respectively, following Q3 earnings.

In Q4, Morgan Stanley expects Software and Consulting gross margins to be flat to lower year-over-year, while it models an improving trajectory in Infrastructure margins on potentially higher enterprise license agreements, the note added.

Morgan Stanley kept an equal-weight rating on IBM and raised its price target to $240 from $238.
